metrics.label: Professional, scientific and technical services, one month
Hiring managers reporting fewer entry-level hires

claims.text: In October 2026 professional and business services added 70,000 jobs against a twelve-month average of 15,000; professional, scientific and technical services alone added 33,000, and the wider sector has added 269,000 jobs since its October 2025 low.

Analysis of the same release finds professional and technical services had its biggest one-month gain since October 2022 — while insurance lost 89,700 jobs over the year (−3.0%), publishing 23,500 (−2.6%) and motion pictures 19,600 (−5.6%), and concludes there is still little evidence of a broad AI effect on employment.
Entry-level roles that now require more than ten traditionally senior skills are growing at 35%, while other entry-level roles decline by around 10%.

The most AI-exposed entry-level roles are seven times more likely than the least exposed to demand traditionally senior skills such as leadership, strategic decision-making and stakeholder management — 52% of the new skills listed, against 7% for the least exposed.

In Northeastern University's AI & Society Survey of 8,174 people with a say in hiring, 26% of those who said AI affected their decisions reported hiring fewer entry-level candidates, against 7% hiring more; 54% use AI to screen résumés, rising to 83% in technology.
49% of CEOs expect AI adoption to decrease junior hiring over the next three years, against 12% for senior hiring.
